incident.what: An hourly heartbeat kept waking an agent whose checks were all green. Each wake ended with a one-line 'all green, standing by' message to the operator — twice in a row on the first day of a session, after the same pattern had been called out earlier that week. The operator's words: 'why are you spinning again'. Meanwhile the agent's own pending ledger held items it could have done alone.
incident.signal: Operator messages consisting only of check results; consecutive rounds whose only content is a status.

root_cause: The rule 'green means silent' was applied to speech but not to work: silence was read as 'nothing to do'. A timer that forces a turn, plus a harness that expects a visible reply per turn, turns every green tick into a message.

law.text: A green tick is silent to the operator and still recorded. Silence is not absence: the ledger round and the tick log are the liveness proof. Nothing is said unless there is a red check, a next item, or new inbox — and 'nothing to say' is never a reason not to draw the next doable item.
checks: a tick with no red check, no next item and no inbox prints nothing on stdout
the round is still appended and logs/tick.log still gets its line
the loop reports a silent tick as nothing, not as 'ok — '

notes: De-identified from a real operating incident. The same agent had recorded the rule in prose three weeks earlier and still broke it — which is why it is now a property of the tick script, not of the agent.
